cast.name: The Happy Prince
cast.role: Gilded statue on a tall column, also called 'the statue' in attributions
cast.description: A statue of the Happy Prince, as tall as a man, standing on a high column above the city square; gilded all over with thin leaves of fine gold, with two bright sapphire eyes and a large ruby glowing on his sword-hilt. Later stripped of his gold so he looks dull and grey, and his leaden heart snaps in the frost. Gentle, weeping, commanding.

cast.name: The Swallow
cast.role: Late-migrating swallow in love with the Reed
cast.description: A small swallow barely larger than a human hand, late to fly to Egypt because he loves a slender-waisted Reed; touches the water with silver ripples in courtship; finally dies of cold at the Prince's feet after kissing him.

cast.name: The Reed
cast.role: Swallow's beloved by the river
cast.description: A slender-waisted Reed rooted in the river, taller than the Swallow but much smaller than a person; bows and curtseys in the wind and shakes her head when asked to travel.

cast.name: The Town Councillors
cast.role: Officials who agree with the Mayor
cast.description: A crowd of formal officials in dark coats who always agree with the Mayor and who melt the Happy Prince.

cast.name: The Charity Children
cast.role: Cathedral children who compare the Prince to an angel
cast.description: A small crowd of clean children in bright scarlet cloaks and white pinafores emerging from the cathedral.

cast.name: The Mathematical Master
cast.role: Severe schoolmaster who dismisses dreams
cast.description: A bald, bespectacled schoolmaster in scholar's robes who frowns severely and tells the Charity Children they have never seen an angel.

cast.name: The Seamstress
cast.role: Poor seamstress who receives the ruby
cast.description: A thin-faced, dark-haired woman in a worn work-dress, with coarse red hands pricked by the needle, sewing passion-flowers by lamplight while her sick boy lies in the corner bed.

cast.name: The Sick Boy
cast.role: Feverish child who craves oranges
cast.description: A small pale boy lying ill in a corner bed; cries for oranges until the Swallow fans his brow, then sinks into slumber.

cast.name: The Student in the Garret
cast.role: Cold playwright who receives the sapphire
cast.description: A young man with brown crisp hair and pomegranate-red lips, leaning over a desk of papers beside a tumbler of withered violets in a cold garret; sells the sapphire and finishes his play.

cast.name: The Match-girl
cast.role: Bare-headed child who receives the second sapphire
cast.description: A little girl with bare head, no shoes or stockings, whose matches have fallen in the gutter; believes the sapphire is a lovely bit of glass and runs home laughing.

cast.name: The Professor of Ornithology
cast.role: Academic who writes about the winter swallow
cast.description: A bespectacled University scholar who crosses the bridge, marvels 'A swallow in winter!', and writes a long letter full of unintelligible words to the local newspaper.

cast.name: The Foundry Overseer
cast.role: Workman who finds the lead heart will not melt
cast.description: A workman in cap and dark apron at the foundry, surprised that the Prince's broken lead heart cannot be melted in the furnace.

cast.name: The Nightingale
cast.role: Brown nightingale who gives her life for a rose
cast.description: A small nightingale with brown wings who nests in a holm-oak; hears the Student's grief, decides he is a true lover, and presses her breast all night to a thorn until a crimson rose blooms and she dies.

cast.name: The Young Student
cast.role: Student of philosophy who wants a red rose
cast.description: A pale, slim young man with hair dark as hyacinth-blossom and lips red as a rose; face like ivory, sorrow on his brow; reads dusty philosophy books in his room.

cast.name: The Professor's Daughter
cast.role: The girl who rejects the red rose
cast.description: A young woman with long fair hair, in a light dress, sitting in the doorway winding blue silk on a reel with a little dog at her feet; prefers the Chamberlain's nephew's real jewels to a flower.

cast.name: The Holm-Oak
cast.role: Tree in which the Nightingale nests
cast.description: A tall holm-oak in whose branches the Nightingale has built her nest; many times taller than a person; gentle and fond of the little bird.

cast.name: The Three Rose-trees
cast.role: White, yellow, and red Rose-trees of the Student's garden
cast.description: Three rose-trees, each as tall as a person, grouped as one: a white one on the grass-plot, a yellow one at the old sun-dial, and a red one beneath the Student's window. The red one, winter-chilled, yields a single crimson rose after the Nightingale's sacrifice.

cast.name: The Selfish Giant
cast.role: Giant owner of the walled garden
cast.description: A very tall, heavy, broad-shouldered elder giant with long white hair and a long white beard, in a robe; returns from seven years with the Cornish ogre, walls out the children, then melts, knocks down the wall, and dies under a tree of white blossoms.

cast.name: The Children
cast.role: Schoolchildren who play in the Giant's garden
cast.description: A crowd of schoolchildren in everyday clothes who play in the garden, are driven out, creep back through a hole, and finally find the Giant dead.

cast.name: Snow
cast.role: Personified Snow that covers the garden
cast.description: A spirit the size of a person who covers the Giant's grass with her great white cloak and cries that Spring has forgotten the garden.

cast.name: Frost
cast.role: Personified Frost that paints the trees silver
cast.description: A spirit the size of a person who paints all the trees silver and joins Snow in bringing endless winter.

cast.name: The North Wind
cast.role: Personified Wind invited by Snow and Frost
cast.description: A great spirit wrapped in furs who roars all day and blows the chimney-pots down; declares the garden a delightful spot and invites the Hail.

cast.name: The Hail
cast.role: Personified Hail that rattles on the roof
cast.description: A spirit in grey with icy breath who rattles on the castle roof for three hours and runs round the garden; a perfect monster with no hesitation.

cast.name: The Water-rat
cast.role: Old bachelor who debates friendship
cast.description: An old water-rat the size of a small mammal, with bright beady eyes, stiff grey whiskers, and a long tail like black india-rubber; lives alone by the pond and is fond of fiction.

cast.name: The Duck (of the Pond)
cast.role: Mother duck with ducklings
cast.description: A pure white duck with real red legs and yellow ducklings, larger than a water-rat; teaches her children to stand on their heads and supplies the final moral about stories with morals.

cast.name: The Green Linnet
cast.role: Storyteller of Hans's tale
cast.description: A small green linnet who swings on silver sprays and flaps tiny wings; tells The Devoted Friend to the Water-rat and concludes that telling a story with a moral is dangerous.

cast.name: Hans
cast.role: Kind little gardener, devoted friend
cast.description: A short, slight, light-haired man with a funny round good-humoured face, in a work-apron; the most devoted friend of big Hugh the Miller; finally drowned on the moor.

cast.name: The Miller (Big Hugh)
cast.role: Rich selfish neighbour of Hans
cast.description: A very tall, broad, heavy miller in dark shirt and trousers, with a hundred sacks of flour and six milch cows; talks beautifully about unselfish friendship while taking everything from Hans.

cast.name: The Miller's Wife
cast.role: Flattery-loving wife of the Miller
cast.description: A comfortable woman in a long dress, seated in an armchair by the big pinewood fire, pouring herself warm ale; praises the Miller's friendship speeches.

cast.name: The Miller's Youngest Son
cast.role: Sympathetic child who wants to share with Hans
cast.description: A small boy with white rabbits at home, who offers Hans half his porridge and is silenced by his father as untaught.

cast.name: The Remarkable Rocket
cast.role: Proud firework tied to a long stick
cast.description: A tall, supercilious rocket the height of a small child, tied to the end of a long stick; coughs before speaking and believes himself the centre of every occasion. Damp with his own tears at the display; finally exploded alone in daylight.

cast.name: The Roman Candle
cast.role: Big, blunt, practical firework
cast.description: A big Roman candle among the fireworks, taller and thicker than the squibs; calls the Rocket's romanticism humbug and tells him to keep himself dry.

cast.name: The Frog
cast.role: Green ditch-dweller who croaks to the Rocket
cast.description: A small green mottled frog with bright jewelled eyes, who loves rainy weather and talks of his glee-club in the old duck pond; has six beautiful daughters.

cast.name: The White Duck
cast.role: Practical-minded duck in the ditch
cast.description: A great white duck with yellow legs and webbed feet, considered a beauty for her waddle; once took the chair at a reform meeting but now goes in for domesticity.

cast.name: The Small Fire-balloon
cast.role: Cheerful firework who soars to tell the stars
cast.description: A small fire-balloon among the fireworks, who soars up into the air dropping tiny blue sparks and intends to tell the stars all about the bride.

cast.name: The King
cast.role: Royal father of the bridegroom, bad flute-player
cast.description: An old king in ermine robes and a gold crown, who plays the flute very badly and knows only two airs; doubles the Page's salary for flattering his playing.

cast.name: The King's Son
cast.role: The bridegroom of the Russian Princess
cast.description: A young royal prince with hair like fine gold and dreamy violet eyes; kneels to the Princess in his father's palace.

cast.name: The Russian Princess
cast.role: Pale bride who has never seen fireworks
cast.description: A pale Russian Princess in an ermine cloak and silver-tissue cap, who has lived all her life in a Snow Palace and blushes like a red rose when complimented.

cast.name: The Two Boys
cast.role: Country boys who burn the Rocket
cast.description: Two little boys in white smocks with a kettle and faggots, who mistake the Rocket for an old stick and put him on the fire to boil the kettle.

cast.name: The Bengal Light
cast.role: Firework who corrects spelling and bullies squibs
cast.description: A small Bengal Light among the fireworks; corrects the Rocket's spelling of Pyrotechnic and bullies the squibs to show his importance.

cast.name: The little Squib
cast.role: Naive little firework
cast.description: A little Squib who marvels at the yellow tulips and believes travel improves the mind.

cast.name: The pensive Catherine Wheel
cast.role: Romantic, melancholic firework
cast.description: A pensive Catherine Wheel attached to an old deal box in early life, who mourns that Romance is dead and sighs over the Rocket's weeping.

cast.name: The Cracker
cast.role: Firework politician
cast.description: A Cracker with political leanings who calls 'Order! order!' and nearly explodes with laughter.

cast.name: The Dragon-fly
cast.role: Insect on the bulrush
cast.description: A Dragon-fly with lovely gauze wings who sits on a large brown bulrush in the ditch and tells the Rocket to lecture on Philosophy.

cast.name: The young Page
cast.role: Courtier who notes the Princess's colour
cast.description: A young Page at the King's court who notices the Princess blushes from white to red and whose salary is doubled (from nothing).

cast.name: The Doctor
cast.role: Doctor summoned on the stormy night
cast.description: A Doctor who comes out of his house in big boots with his horse and lantern.

cast.name: The Mayor
cast.role: Stout city Mayor who leads the council
cast.description: The city Mayor, a heavy-set man in a dark long coat and top hat who walks the square with his councillors.

locations.name: The City Square
locations.description: The square beneath the tall column on which the Happy Prince stands; the Mayor walks here with the Town Councillors.

locations.name: The Seamstress's Room
locations.description: A poor room in a little street with a corner bed for the sick boy and a table where the seamstress embroiders passion-flowers.

locations.name: The Student's Garret
locations.description: A cold attic room with a hole in the roof, a desk covered in papers, and a tumbler of withered violets.

locations.name: The Palace
locations.description: The royal Palace of Sans-Souci in the Prince's memory and the King's Palace where the wedding is held, with a balcony overlooking the square.

locations.name: The River and Harbour
locations.description: The river through the city with the harbour at its mouth, where ships' lanterns hang from their masts and the Professor crosses the bridge.

locations.name: The Foundry
locations.description: The furnace room where the statue is melted; its dustheap outside receives the lead heart and the dead Swallow.

locations.name: The Student's Garden
locations.description: A walled garden with a grass-plot, a sun-dial, the Student's window, and three rose-trees of different colours, surrounded by a grove.

locations.name: The Giant's Garden
locations.description: A large lovely garden with soft green grass, twelve peach-trees, and birds; walled all round by the Giant with a 'TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED' notice. In winter it lies under snow and frost; in spring the trees blossom.

locations.name: The Pond
locations.description: A pond with a willow-tree on the bank where the Water-rat, Duck, and Linnet meet to discuss friendship.

locations.name: Hans's Cottage
locations.description: A tiny cottage all by itself with a lovely garden of Sweet-william, Gilly-flowers, Roses, and Violets; a porch where Hans nails honeysuckle.

locations.name: The Miller's Mill
locations.description: A windmill up the hill with sails tied by an iron chain, a great cask of red wine, and a barn with a hole in the roof.

locations.name: The Moor
locations.description: A dangerous open moor beyond the road, full of deep holes, where Hans loses his way and drowns.

locations.name: The King's Garden Firework Stand
locations.description: The end of the King's garden where a great stand is set up at midnight and the fireworks are displayed.

locations.name: The Ditch by the Country Road
locations.description: A muddy ditch beside a country road where the Rocket lands after being thrown over the wall and is found by two boys with a kettle.
